propositions.name: species_descended_like_varieties
propositions.quote: each species had not been independently created, but had descended, like varieties, from other species
propositions.statement: Each species has not been independently created but has descended, like varieties, from other species.

propositions.name: external_conditions_inadequate_woodpecker
propositions.quote: it is preposterous to attribute to mere external conditions, the structure, for instance, of the woodpecker, with its feet, tail, beak, and tongue, so admirably adapted to catch insects under the bark of trees
propositions.statement: External conditions alone cannot account for the adaptive structure of the woodpecker's feet, tail, beak, and tongue for catching insects under bark.

propositions.name: domestication_best_clue
propositions.quote: a careful study of domesticated animals and of cultivated plants would offer the best chance of making out this obscure problem
propositions.statement: Careful study of domesticated animals and cultivated plants offers the best chance of understanding the means of modification.

propositions.name: hereditary_modification_possible
propositions.quote: a large amount of hereditary modification is at least possible
propositions.statement: A large amount of hereditary modification is at least possible.

propositions.name: mans_selection_accumulates_variations
propositions.quote: how great is the power of man in accumulating by his Selection successive slight variations
propositions.statement: Man has great power to accumulate successive slight variations by his Selection.

propositions.name: struggle_from_geometrical_increase
propositions.quote: the Struggle for Existence amongst all organic beings throughout the world, which inevitably follows from their high geometrical powers of increase
propositions.statement: A struggle for existence among all organic beings follows inevitably from their high geometrical powers of increase.

propositions.name: malthus_applies_to_all_life
propositions.quote: This is the doctrine of Malthus, applied to the whole animal and vegetable kingdoms
propositions.statement: The Malthusian doctrine applies to the whole animal and vegetable kingdoms.

propositions.name: overproduction_of_offspring
propositions.quote: As many more individuals of each species are born than can possibly survive; and as, consequently, there is a frequently recurring struggle for existence
propositions.statement: Many more individuals of each species are born than can possibly survive, so a struggle for existence recurs frequently.

propositions.name: profitable_variation_selected
propositions.quote: any being, if it vary however slightly in any manner profitable to itself, under the complex and sometimes varying conditions of life, will have a better chance of surviving, and thus be naturally selected
propositions.statement: Any being that varies however slightly in a manner profitable to itself will have a better chance of surviving and be naturally selected.

propositions.name: strong_principle_of_inheritance
propositions.quote: From the strong principle of inheritance, any selected variety will tend to propagate its new and modified form
propositions.statement: By the strong principle of inheritance, any selected variety will tend to propagate its new and modified form.

propositions.name: selection_causes_extinction_and_divergence
propositions.quote: Natural Selection almost inevitably causes much Extinction of the less improved forms of life, and induces what I have called Divergence of Character
propositions.statement: Natural Selection almost inevitably causes much Extinction of the less improved forms and induces Divergence of Character.

propositions.name: transitions_from_simple_to_complex
propositions.quote: how a simple being or a simple organ can be changed and perfected into a highly developed being or elaborately constructed organ
propositions.statement: A simple being or organ must be capable of being changed and perfected into a highly developed being or elaborately constructed organ.

propositions.name: hybridism_species_variety_distinction
propositions.quote: Hybridism, or the infertility of species and the fertility of varieties when intercrossed
propositions.statement: Species are infertile and varieties fertile when intercrossed, and this Hybridism is a difficulty for the theory.

propositions.name: geological_succession_of_beings
propositions.quote: In the next chapter I shall consider the geological succession of organic beings throughout time
propositions.statement: Organic beings exhibit a geological succession throughout time that must be accounted for.

propositions.name: classification_reflects_affinities
propositions.quote: their classification or mutual affinities, both when mature and in an embryonic condition
propositions.statement: The classification or mutual affinities of organic beings, both mature and embryonic, are evidence to be explained.

propositions.name: independent_creation_erroneous
propositions.quote: the view which most naturalists entertain, and which I formerly entertained—namely, that each species has been independently created—is erroneous
propositions.statement: The view that each species has been independently created is erroneous.

propositions.name: species_not_immutable
propositions.quote: species are not immutable; but that those belonging to what are called the same genera are lineal descendants of some other and generally extinct species
propositions.statement: Species are not immutable; those of the same genera are lineal descendants of other and generally extinct species.

propositions.name: natural_selection_main_not_exclusive
propositions.quote: Natural Selection has been the main but not exclusive means of modification
propositions.statement: Natural Selection has been the main but not the exclusive means of modification.

propositions.name: present_relations_govern_future_modification
propositions.quote: these relations are of the highest importance, for they determine the present welfare, and, as I believe, the future success and modification of every inhabitant of this world
propositions.statement: Mutual relations among beings determine present welfare and the future success and modification of every inhabitant of the world.
